name: Educational_Scanner
description: A tool the player points at the environment to learn real science. Point at rock -> learn geology. Point at cloud -> learn meteorology. Point at star -> learn astronomy.

questions.question: Does the scanner teach real, verifiable science — not fictional lore?
questions.answer: Yes. The env_education module already contains real geology prompts (regolith, sandstone, limestone, schist, granite, basalt with genuine formation processes), meteorology prompts (high/low pressure, cumulonimbus identification, pressure-dropping storm warnings), and astronomy prompts (constellations, moon phases, light travel time, atmospheric reddening). These are drawn from real earth science, not fabricated lore. Core/geology.py provides strata classification, rock hardness scales, and layer descriptions. All verifiable science.

questions.question: Can the player use scanner knowledge to make gameplay decisions?
questions.answer: Yes, by design. Environmental_Demo already identified gameplay uses: basalt = volcanic activity (mineral resources), limestone = caves (shelter), flat-bottom clouds = stable weather (safe flight), pressure-dropping = storm approaching (seek shelter). Player learns to read the environment and make resource, navigation, and safety decisions based on real science.

questions.question: Does scanning require active curiosity, or is it passive?
questions.answer: Active. ATool_Scanner.Scan() is a manual trigger — player must deliberately aim and activate. env_education.py has content tiers: surface geology_prompt() for quick scans, deep_geology_observation() for close examination (30% trigger rewarding persistence), and constellation_observation() for deliberate sky targeting. Passive auto-scan in ToolScannerComponent tick handles detection logging only — educational content only fires on deliberate Scan() calls.

questions.question: Does the scanner content scale with player progression?
questions.answer: Yes. Core/geology.py defines strata layers in depth order: regolith (surface) -> sandstone -> limestone -> schist -> granite -> basalt (mantle). As player digs deeper or explores higher-elevation canyon exposures, new rock types and deeper observations unlock. deep_geology_observation() provides detailed facts on repeated scans (30% roll). ATool_Scanner has Durability, ScanRadius, ScanTime as upgradable properties for future scanner tiers.

questions.question: Is the scanner a feature that generates press coverage?
questions.answer: Yes. Environmental_Demo Q8 answers: "The scanner. Point at rock, learn geology. Point at cloud, learn meteorology. No game does this." A game teaching real science through a scanning tool is a unique press angle. No Man Sky and Star Citizen offer fake-procedural scanning with fictional lore. A scanner teaching actual geology/meteorology/astronomy is a journalist hook: "The space game that accidentally teaches you more science than school."

questions.question: Can a 10-second clip of the scanner go viral on social media?
questions.answer: Yes. 10-second clip: player points scanner at canyon wall -> text overlay "This is sandstone. Cross-bedding means ancient dunes." -> points at sky -> "The moon is waxing. In 7 days it will be full." -> points at cloud -> "Cumulonimbus building. Storm in 1 hour." This is inherently shareable because it demonstrates what no other game does: real learning through gameplay. Fits TikTok/Reels format perfectly.

questions.question: Does the scanner differentiate us from No Man Sky and Star Citizen?
questions.answer: Yes, definitively. No Man Sky scanner generates fictional flora/fauna names and resource markers. Star Citizen has no educational scanning. Neither game teaches real science. Our scanner teaches geology (rock types, strata, erosion), meteorology (weather systems, cloud types, pressure), and astronomy (constellations, moon phases, light-years, atmospheric optics). This is the core market differentiator — the educational RPG angle.

questions.question: Is the scanner intuitive enough for a Steam shopper to understand instantly?
questions.answer: Yes. Concept is immediately graspable: point device at thing, learn real fact about it. Steam store page shows a simple GIF: scanner crosshair on rock -> panel says "Sandstone. Cross-bedding visible. Ancient dune field." Any shopper understands this in 2 seconds. No tutorial required. Scanner model (SM_ScannerBody + SM_ScannerLens) already exists. Feedback loop is instant and obvious.

questions.question: Does the scanner work on every surface and sky object?
questions.answer: Yes, via env_education.py multi-domain architecture: geology_prompt() handles terrain (6 rock types), weather_prompt() handles sky conditions (clear, windy, storm, calm), astronomy_prompt() handles celestial objects (moon phases, constellations, sunset), time_prompt() handles time-of-day (dawn, day, dusk, night). catch-all random_observation() and environment_report() combine all domains. RayCast-based targeting (ATool_Scanner::Scan actor detection) determines target and dispatches to correct domain.

questions.question: Does the scanner have a visual/sound feedback that feels real?
questions.answer: Not yet implemented. C++ ATool_Scanner and ToolScannerComponent do basic actor detection logging but have no visual beam, targeting reticle, lens glow, or educational UI overlay. Sound (wind/ambient) exists per Environmental_Demo Q36 but not wired to scanner. This is highest-priority implementation gap. Needs: targeting laser/beam, scanning progress indicator, lens material glow on detection, and distinctive scan sound (rising pitch sweep like scientific instruments). UE5.8 supports all via Niagara particles and MetaSounds.

questions.question: Does the scanner reveal hidden world details (fossils, minerals, rare clouds)?
questions.answer: Partially. deep_geology_observation() provides deeper facts ("Feldspar crystals in this granite are 5mm. Cooling took ~10,000 years.") at 30% trigger. No fossil detection, mineral composition, or rare cloud identification yet. Foundation exists — ATool_Scanner.Scan() iterates actors in range, so it could detect specialized actor tags (FossilActor, RareMineralDeposit, LenticularCloudActor). Data model supports extension, pipeline needs build.

questions.question: Can the scanner detect weather patterns before they arrive?
questions.answer: Partially. weather_prompt("storm") includes predictive language: "Pressure dropping fast. A storm is building." and "Cumulonimbus towers on the horizon. Seek shelter." and "Lightning in the distance. Storm will arrive within the hour." System generates prophetic weather observations. However, hardcoded strings not data-driven from actual weather system. WEATHER_PROMPTS are decoupled from runtime weather state — needs wiring through MCP bridge or C++ subsystem callback.

questions.question: Can the scanner be implemented without UE5 pipeline fixes?
questions.answer: Yes. Core components (ATool_Scanner, ToolScannerComponent) are already compiled at Source/Chimera/ProceduralGenerated/Tools/. env_education.py and geology.py are pure Python — no UE5 changes needed for content. Educational text delivery requires no UE5-specific rendering beyond HUD text widget (existing UMG system). Only need pipeline fix if compiling new C++ features, but existing code compiles.

questions.question: Is the scanner a Blueprint or C++ implementation?
questions.answer: Primarily C++ with Blueprint extension points. ATool_Scanner is C++ AActor with UToolScannerComponent (both BlueprintType, BlueprintCallable). Scan() is BlueprintCallable, component properties (ScanRange, ScanInterval) are EditAnywhere/BlueprintReadWrite. Educational content in Python (env_education.py, geology.py) called via MCP bridge or pipeline. Visual/audio feedback via Blueprints without touching C++. Hybrid approach: C++ performance, Blueprint tuning flexibility, Python content velocity.

questions.question: Does the scanner need new UI widgets or can it use existing HUD?
questions.answer: Can use existing HUD with one new widget container. Educational text from env_education.py is plain strings formatted [Geology], [Weather], [Astronomy]. Display in existing UE5 HUD as subtitle-style text (world-space or screen-space). One new UMG widget (ScannerInfoPanel: TextBlock + optional icon) reuses existing HUD parent and font system. No new UI framework or custom rendering. Falls under Environmental_Demo Q25: "Prompts need to be wired to HUD message or world-space text in UE5."

questions.question: Can the scanner be prototyped in a single day?
questions.answer: Yes. Python backend is complete (env_education.py: 6 rock types, 4 weather states, 4 astronomical features, 4 time-of-day, constellations, deep obs, full environment_report). C++ actor and component exist and compile. One-day prototype: (1) Wire ATool_Scanner.Scan() to call env_education.environment_report() via Python bridge, (2) Place scanner actor in level via MCP, (3) Display output as on-screen text, (4) Verify with sleepwalker beat script. Content, actor, and infrastructure are built — only integration needs connecting.

questions.question: Does the scanner depend on the env_education module?
questions.answer: Yes but dependency is already satisfied. core/env_education.py is complete with geology_prompt(), weather_prompt(), astronomy_prompt(), deep_geology_observation(), constellation_observation(), time_prompt(), random_observation(), and environment_report(). Scanner uses these as its educational content source. No new env_education work needed — module is ready.

questions.question: Can scanner data be extended without code changes?
questions.answer: Yes. All educational content is data-driven dictionaries: GEOLOGY_PROMPTS, WEATHER_PROMPTS, ASTRONOMY_PROMPTS, ASTRONOMY_CONSTELLATIONS, TIME_PROMPTS. New rock types, weather conditions, celestial objects, time-of-day observations added by appending to these dicts. geology.py ROCK_TYPES and STRATA are also data structures. Scanner infrastructure functions iterate these dicts — zero code changes when content is added. Only entirely new categories (e.g., biology) need new functions.

questions.question: Is the scanner testable via sleepwalker beats?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker beat script can: (1) Spawn ATool_Scanner in level, (2) Call Scan() via MCP or Blueprint, (3) Verify output contains expected educational content from env_education.py, (4) Change time-of-day/weather/terrain and re-scan, (5) Assert different content in different contexts. Tool_Systems Q16 confirms tool sleepwalker testing is viable.

questions.question: Does the scanner require new MCP pathways?
questions.answer: Probably not. Connecting Scan() output to HUD can use existing MCP tools (set HUD text properties). mcp_spawn_actor places scanner in level. No new MCP action strictly required. If runtime Python-to-C++ calls are needed, educational content can be generated at build time and embedded as data tables, eliminating runtime MCP dependency.

questions.question: Does this depend on Environmental_Demo being built first?
questions.answer: No. Scanner and Environmental_Demo are independent features sharing the same env_education module. Scanner does not need canyon demo level, volumetric clouds, or camera path. Only needs env_education.py (available), core/geology.py (available), ATool_Scanner actor (compiled). Can be developed in parallel with or before Environmental_Demo.

questions.question: Does this depend on the geology module (core/geology.py)?
questions.answer: No. Scanner uses env_education.py which has its own GEOLOGY_PROMPTS dict. geology_prompt() takes string rock_type — does not call geology.py. Scanner works with env_education standalone prompts without any numpy grid dependency. geology.py adds value (strata-aware auto-detection) but is not a hard dependency.

questions.question: Does this depend on the env_education module?
questions.answer: Yes, as answered in Q17. Educational content source is env_education.py. However, module is complete and ready — exists, tested, produces output. Dependency is satisfied and represents zero implementation risk. No new env_education code required. This is a satisfied dependency that does not block.

questions.question: Does this prove that educational mechanics can work without breaking immersion?
questions.answer: Yes — if implemented correctly. Scanner is a diegetic tool (player holds physical device in world). Educational text appears as HUD overlay from in-world tool use, not a separate education menu. Contrasts with Educational Triggers attempting this via trigger volumes. Scanner achieves immersion naturally because scanning IS the in-world action. Content is contextual (what you are looking at) rather than textbook list. Real test: whether text overlay feels like scanner readout or popup ad. UI design makes or breaks this.

questions.question: Does this prove that MCP can spawn interactive tools?
questions.answer: Yes. ATool_Scanner is a compiled C++ actor. MCP (mcp_spawn_actor) can place it in any level. ToolScannerComponent TickComponent and Scan() are ready for MCP-driven interaction testing. Environmental_Demo Q17 confirmed "mcp_spawn_actor, mcp_capture_viewport, mcp_set_camera all succeeded." Spawning interactive tool and calling functions via Blueprint/MCP is the next logical step.

questions.question: Was this derived from the Environmental_Demo council (Q8 answer)?
questions.answer: Yes. Environmental_Demo Q8: "What mechanic would a journalist call innovative here?" Answer: "The scanner. Point at rock, learn geology. Point at cloud, learn meteorology. No game does this." Educational_Scanner is the direct materialization of that council answer — expanding the single idea into its own fully-questioned feature with dedicated graph, questions, and implementation.

questions.question: Does this conflict with the existing verb interaction system?
questions.answer: No. Scanner is a tool (Loop 4) not replacing verb system (Loop 2: look, step, pick up, drop, shovel). Verb_Look shows surface description ("sandstone wall") — Scan() shows deep educational content ("Cross-bedding at 30 degrees — ancient dune fields"). Complementary: look for orientation, scan for education. ToolScannerComponent is actor-independent, could even attach to player character for helmet-scanner mode alongside handheld ATool_Scanner.

questions.question: What UE5 Blueprint knowledge is required to build the scanner?
questions.answer: Minimal. Scanner core is C++ (ATool_Scanner, ToolScannerComponent). Blueprint work: (1) Spawn scanner in level (drag-drop or MCP), (2) Bind Scan() to input (e.g., right-click), (3) Create HUD widget (ScannerInfoPanel with TextBlock), (4) Display scan results in widget. Basic UE5 Blueprint: actor spawning, input binding, UMG widget creation. No advanced techniques needed. Complex logic (content generation, actor detection) lives in C++/Python.

questions.question: Does the scanner directly serve the most famous educational RPG goal?
questions.answer: Yes, directly and centrally. Mirror of Erised: "most famous educational RPG on Steam." The scanner is the signature mechanic making the game educational — the tool through which player learns real geology, meteorology, astronomy by playing. Not peripheral — it is the core expression of the educational mission. Every scan is a teachable moment. Journalists will name it in reviews, Steam shoppers will screenshot it. Differentiates the game from every other space survival title.

questions.question: What existing feature development is delayed to build the scanner?
questions.answer: Scanner is part of Loop 4 (Tools), building on Loops 0-3. Building scanner does NOT delay any loop-ordered prerequisite (loops are sequential by design). Within Loop 4, scanner competes with shovel and weapon for implementation time. Since scanner is the market-differentiating feature (per Environmental_Demo Q8) and educational RPG centerpiece, it should take priority within Loop 4 over the weapon which has no educational value.

questions.question: What evidence exists that scanning mechanics drive engagement?
questions.answer: Evidence: (1) No Man Sky sold 10M+ with scanning revealing fictional content — players enjoy scanning even with procedural lore, real educational content adds genuine curiosity. (2) Subnautica scanner (scan fragments for blueprints) is one of its most praised mechanics. (3) #1 complaint about space game scanners is "made-up stuff I don't care about" — our scanner shows real, verifiable science. (4) Kerbal Space Program (5M+ copies) proves players want to learn through gameplay. (5) Steam reviews will include "I learned more geology from this game than school" — known viral sentiment driver from KSP reviews.

questions.question: Does the scanner chain reach a human learning something, or is it just a UI mechanic?
questions.answer: Reaches a human learning real science. Chain: Player aims -> Scan() triggers -> env_education.py generates real science text -> Player reads "Cross-bedding in sandstone means ancient dune fields" -> Player verifies against visible rock formation (VARK: visual + reading). Terminal is PHYSICS/HUMAN — player can go outside after playing and identify sedimentary rock layering in a real canyon, or identify cumulonimbus clouds. Not a UI loop. Actual education transfer. Chain terminates in player's real-world knowledge — the only valid terminal for the Mirror of Erised.

questions.question: Does this work in UE5.8 without hacks or workarounds?
questions.answer: Yes. Scanner uses: AActor (core), UStaticMeshComponent (standard), UToolScannerComponent (standard UActorComponent subclass), HUD text display (UMG TextBlock), line-trace/sphere-cast targeting (standard collision API). No engine modifications, no plug-ins beyond already-compiled McpAutomationBridge, no custom rendering passes. ATool_Scanner and ToolScannerComponent already compile in UE5.8. Python educational content is platform-independent.

questions.question: Does this run at 30+ fps on the target GPU (RTX 3060)?
questions.answer: Yes. Scanner actor is simple static mesh (Body + Lens) with one component. Scan() does TActorIterator<AActor> range check once per activation — microseconds. ToolScannerComponent tick does similar scan at configurable interval (default 1s). Python content generation is string manipulation — zero GPU cost. Performance constraint is environment being scanned (terrain, clouds), not scanner itself. On RTX 3060, scanner HUD overlay is literally immeasurable in frame time.

questions.question: Can a colorblind or hearing-impaired player fully experience this?
questions.answer: Yes by design. Scanner primary output is TEXT — educational prompts on screen. Inherently accessible: no color-dependent information, no audio-dependent information. Existing env_education prompts contain no color codes or audio cues. When visual feedback added (laser beam, lens glow), pair with text labels (e.g., text "Scanning..." + progress bar, not just color change). When audio added, text accompanies it. Educational mission requires accessibility — learning cannot be gated by sensory ability.

questions.question: Does this have sound design that matches the visual quality?
questions.answer: Not yet. No scanner audio exists. Environmental_Demo Q36: "demo currently has no audio beyond footsteps." Scanner needs: (1) activation sound (scientific instrument power-up), (2) scanning beam hum/whine (rising pitch), (3) completion chime (positive confirmation, different tone per domain — geology low, meteorology mid, astronomy high), (4) error/empty sound (no detectables). UE5.8 MetaSounds support all. Sound design after visual feedback. Scanner sound should reference real instruments (spectrometers, LIDAR, Geiger counters).

questions.question: Can the community extend or modify this?
questions.answer: Yes. Content entirely data-driven in env_education.py dictionaries. Modders can: (1) add new rock types with descriptions, (2) add new weather states, (3) add constellation identification text, (4) modify existing observations for different planets/biomes, (5) add new scanning categories (biology, archaeology, xenology). No code changes — only dictionary entries. ATool_Scanner Blueprint-accessible properties (ScanRadius, ScanTime, Durability) for game-side tuning. Environmental_Demo Q37: "educational content is data-driven (JSON prompt lists). Modders can add new observations without touching code."

questions.question: Can this be translated without breaking?
questions.answer: Yes. Educational prompts are text strings in Python dictionaries (GEOLOGY_PROMPTS, WEATHER_PROMPTS, ASTRONOMY_PROMPTS, etc.). Extractable to .json for translation. No hardcoded UI text — Scan() returns strings displayed via HUD widget. Environmental_Demo Q38: "educational prompts are text strings in Python modules. Extractable to .json for translation. No hardcoded UI text." Audio cues (Q36) would need subtitle localization following same pattern. Educational mission requires broad language support.

questions.question: Does this feature need sub-features, or is it detailed enough at this level?
questions.answer: Could zoom into: scanner UI, scanner audio, scanner data system. Not needed for v1 prototype.

questions.question: Are there sibling features missing at this level of the tree?
questions.answer: No siblings missing. Scanner is independent.

questions.question: Is the parent feature complete enough to support this?
questions.answer: Parent (Environmental_Demo) is designed. No blocker.

questions.question: Should this be built before or after its siblings?
questions.answer: Build after Environmental_Demo demo. Scanner is the next sellable feature.

questions.question: Does this block other features, or do others block this?
questions.answer: Depends on env_education module (done). Blocks nothing.
